newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Weekend Zaire talks might be delayed - S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Weekend Zaire talks might be delayed - S.Africa.

text.p: Talks in South Africa aimed at bringing peace to Zaire could be delayed by the latest political developments in Kinshasa, a senior South African diplomat said on Friday.
"Maybe there will be...a later date that will be set aside for the discussions," said Happy Mahlangu, South Africa's deputy high commissioner in London in an interview with the BBC.

On the eve of the talks, rebel leader Laurent Kabila rejected a power-sharing offer from new Zairean Prime Minister Etienne Tshisekedi. Mahlangu said this development threatened to unravel the process.
"On our side, what we needed to do was facilitate the discussions and of course there won't be any discussions if the two parties are not there," he said.

The Zaire government's negotiating team is already in South Africa, meeting officials to discuss arrangements for the talks, but there has been no official confirmation that representatives of the rebels have arrived.
Foreign Affairs Ministry officials in Pretoria declined to comment on Mahlangu's statements.
